# Uppādanirodhavāra (Ya 5.2.3)

**ID:** Ya 5.2.3
**Section:** Yamaka (ya)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Uppādanirodhavāra
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m4.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uppādanirodhavāra* ("Section on Arising and Cessation") is the third subdivision of the process section (*pavattivāra*, Ya 5.2) within the *Saccayamaka* (Ya 5) of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Anderson 1999; Ronkin 2005]. Within this framework, the *pavattivāra* investigates the circumstances of an individual being reborn or passing away in various existential planes [Anderson 1999]. In the *Uppādanirodhavāra*, the four noble truths (*cattāri ariyasaccāni*) are interrogated using paired catechisms to determine how each truth arises, ceases, or both arises and ceases in relation to the other truths across the temporal divisions of the present, past, and future [Anderson 1999].

**Sources**

- [Anderson 1999] Carol S. Anderson, Pain and its Ending: The Four Noble Truths in the Theravāda Buddhist Canon (1999) — Structural description of the Pavattivāra of the Saccayamaka, its threefold division, and question formulas concerning the four truths
- [Gal 2003] Noa Gal, Metaphysics of Experience: From the Buddha's Teaching to the Abhidhamma (2003) — Analysis of the Process section in Yamaka chapters, process metaphysics, and the origin of momentariness (khaṇa)
- [Ronkin 2005] Noa Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics: The Making of a Philosophical Tradition (2005) — Discussion of Yamaka process sections, origination-cessation, and subdivision of moments into uppādakkhaṇa and bhaṅgakkhaṇa
